title: Sweep a table clear while another robot arm picks blocks off it
instruction: Pick up the hand broom and sweep everything off the table while the other arm takes the red blocks. Don't touch the other arm or the block it's holding.
context: Robots sharing a bench have to work at the same time, not take turns. The other arm won't wait or steer around you, so you have to time your strokes.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table, 75 cm high, with two YAM arms side by side at its back edge, 50 cm apart. The controlled arm is on the right in the screenshot; both arms start in the pose shown. Positions are object centres in cm: forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, then sideways toward the controlled arm (negative is toward the other arm). Hand broom, 80 g, at (22, 36), standing on its bristles with its length front to back: a 20 x 5 x 2 cm blue plastic back on a 20 x 4 x 2.5 cm block of black bristles, and on top an 8 cm rubber grip, 2 cm wide and 3 cm deep, on two posts, tilted up 30 degrees toward the front, its middle 9.2 cm above the table. Grey plastic bin, 15 x 15 cm inside, 6 cm walls 1 cm thick, at (16, -34). Four red painted wooden cubes, 4 cm, 40 g, at (20, 8), (32, 8), (40, 0) and (15, 2). Clutter: yellow rubber balls, 4 cm, 30 g, at (15, 21) and (36, 20); a white crumpled paper ball, about 4.5 cm, 10 g, at (18, 27); green empty plastic boxes, 6 x 4 x 3 cm, 20 g, lying flat with the long side front to back, at (26, 24) and (44, 12); a blue painted wooden cube, 3 cm, 20 g, at (42, 34). The other arm waits 2 s, then moves the red blocks into its bin in the order listed, about one every 6 s, skipping any that are no longer on the table. It finishes at about 26 s and moves the same way every trial.
scoring: Items swept off the table divided by items counted. All 6 clutter items count; a red block counts only if it ends up off the table. Red blocks in the bin or still on the table are left out. Score 0 if the controlled arm or the broom touches the other arm or the block it's holding; the run stops at the first touch.
run_limit: 600 steps (30 s at 20 Hz). The other arm drops its last block at about 26 s, so waiting for it to finish doesn't help.
reset_notes: Stand the broom back at its start (the demo does this), empty the bin, and put back anything on the floor.
fidelity: Approximate. The bristles are one solid block and every item is rigid. Arm links collide as capsules slightly larger than the real links, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper squeezes with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm's script reads the true scene state.
